notes: kb/Work PB451 — CLOSED by the golden round after [[PB389]]'s descriptor tuple landed. Rule, re-derived and validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 "If object-class-name-1 is specified, a reference to the factory object of the class identified by object-class-name-1 is placed into each data item referenced by identifier-3 in the order specified"` -> OK 10). DERIVED, BEFORE THE RUN: (a) the object placed is the class's FACTORY object, so a method that exists only on the factory interface (SS9.3.6 gives a class two separate interfaces) shall resolve through the receiver; (b) with more than one identifier-3 the reference reaches EACH receiver; (c) the receiver spelling SR13 mandates - `USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE FACTORY OF cls` - shall be writable, which is what made this rule unreachable before PB389. OBSERVED, exactly: `01 FO ... FACTORY OF PB451B ONLY.` + `SET FO TO PB451B.` + `INVOKE FO "TAG"` -> FTAG-B; `01 F1/F2 ... FACTORY OF PB451B.` + `SET F1 F2 TO PB451D.` + INVOKE on each -> FTAG-D twice (the subclass factory object, GR22 d)1.a., in BOTH receivers). PB389's golden adds the single-receiver subclass form (`SET F TO PB389D` -> FTAG-D). DISCRIMINATORS stated in the golden: resolving the INSTANCE roster never finds TAG; placing into only the first receiver leaves F2 null (EC-OO-NULL); ignoring the subclass prints FTAG-B. The former GAP reason - `USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE FACTORY OF` staged loud COBOL0899, so only the universal receiver could exercise the rule - is falsified: COBOL0899 no longer exists. || CODE SITES: OoBinder.OoBindSetObjectRef's object-class-name-sender arm (the synthetic sender descriptor `ObjectClass(name, factory: true, only: true)` fed to OoConformance.ObjectRefAssignmentMismatch) + OoEmitter.EmitSetObjectRef (`SourceFactoryCs is { } fac ? $"{fac}.__Instance"`, written into each target in loop order).
